claim: *Where engineering leverage acts.* When engineers write most implementation directly, much of their engineering leverage acts through the code. When agents provide abundant realization capacity, more of that leverage moves into the governed engineering environment—the software analogue of the models, fabrication constraints, process instructions, and acceptance criteria surrounding a 3D printer. The environment becomes one means through which engineers retain control while delegating realization: it represents important engineering intent, constrains realization, and evaluates what the fleet produces. MAGE further contends that a governed engineering environment must become the primary means through which engineers exercise control as realization is increasingly delegated.

topology.description: Two comparable production pipelines; engineering leverage moves upstream to environment.

alt: Two production chains are stacked. Classical engineering runs from engineer to implementation to product. Agentic engineering inserts an engineered environment and agents before implementation. Separate text identifies implementation as the classical engineered object and the environment as the agentic lever. Models, obligations, evidence, controls and infrastructure describe that environment. Gray fills distinguish the source semantic roles; labels and line conventions retain their meanings.
